# A consumer cannot resolve the parse5 bundle: dist is npmignored

Refs #17942 · #17921

## Context

Split out of #17942, which fixes the `dist/esm` resolution guard so the **engine's own** build can exit 0. One of the findings that guard surfaced does not close inside that ticket, and #17942 states the bound rather than asserting past it:

`src/functional/util/HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs:3` statically imports `../../../dist/parse5.mjs`. #17942 copies that bundle into `dist/esm/dist/parse5.mjs` when it is present, which is the whole fix **in this repository**. In an installed engine it is never present, and cannot be produced.

## The Problem

Three facts, each measured at `dev`, that compose into an unresolvable import for every consumer:

| fact | evidence |
|---|---|
| `dist/` is excluded from the published package | `.npmignore:71` — `/dist`, with no negation restoring any part of it (`grep '^!' .npmignore` lists only `apps/**` entries) |
| the bundle is a build artifact, not a source file | `buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs:15` writes it via esbuild from `node_modules/parse5/dist/index.js`; `dist/` is gitignored |
| a consumer cannot run that build | `parse5` and `esbuild` are both **devDependencies**, so an installed engine has neither the artifact nor its inputs |

So a workspace that installs `neo.mjs` and runs `dist/esm` copies `HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs` into its output, and that file imports a bundle nothing can put there. Before #17921 the build exited 0 over the dangling import and the failure waited until a runtime that reached the template processor; after it, the build reds. The guard changed when it is discovered, not whether it is broken.

**It is worse than an unresolvable emitted import, and this was measured rather than predicted.** Removing `dist/parse5.mjs` and running the build does not produce a guard report at all — the process dies before it starts:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '…/dist/parse5.mjs'
  imported from …/buildScripts/util/templateBuildProcessor.mjs
```

`esmodules.mjs` imports `astTemplateProcessor`, which imports `templateBuildProcessor`, which imports the bundle at module scope. So the bundle is a hard prerequisite of **running the `dist/esm` build**, not merely of the tree it emits — and an installed engine has no copy of it. Any option below must satisfy the build-time consumer inside the installed package as well as the runtime one.

**This was invisible until a full-engine build ran.** @neo-opus-vega's consumer-workspace receipt (#17942 context) counted it among the survivors; the engine-side build reproduces it from the other direction.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/functional/util/HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs:3` — the consumer of the artifact, and the only `src/` file that reaches outside the source roots.
- `buildScripts/util/templateBuildProcessor.mjs:2` imports the same bundle, but that is a **build-time** consumer inside this repository, where it exists. The runtime consumer is the one with no path to it.
- `buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs` / `package.json` `bundle-parse5` — the producer.
- `buildScripts/build/all.mjs:135` bundles parse5 as part of `build-all`, so the engine's own pipeline always has it.
- This is the same family as #17868 (dependencies resolved by filesystem path rather than module resolution) — a source file reaching a location instead of a package.

## The Fix

The decision is which of these, and it has a release surface, which is why it is not folded into #17942:

1. **Publish the artifact.** Add a negation for `dist/parse5.mjs` in `.npmignore`, and ensure the release build produces it before packing. Smallest change; adds ~170 KB to the tarball and puts a build output in the published tree, which interacts with #17238.
2. **Promote the dependency and import the package.** Move `parse5` to `dependencies` and have `HtmlTemplateProcessor` import it by package name, leaving the bundle to build tooling. Correct by module resolution; adds a runtime dependency to every consumer and changes what the browser has to resolve.
3. **Make the import lazy and optional.** `HtmlTemplateProcessor` obtains parse5 on first use and fails with a diagnostic when absent, so a workspace that never uses `html` templates is unaffected. Largest behavioural change, and it makes a capability conditional that is currently unconditional.

A fourth option — leave it and exempt the specifier — is rejected below.

### Decision (2026-08-31): **Option 1 — publish the artifact.** Options 2 and 3 are rejected on measurement, not preference.

**Option 2 (promote \`parse5\` to \`dependencies\`, import by package name) — REJECTED, infeasible without a new capability.** \`parse5@8.0.1\` is \`type: module\`, and its internal modules import **\`entities/decode\`** and **\`entities/escape\`** — Node *exports-map subpaths*, which no browser resolves without an import map. \`dist/esm\` rewrites path-shaped \`node_modules/…\` specifiers (\`esmDistTransforms.mjs#rewriteImportPaths\`); it does not resolve exports maps, emit import maps, or copy arbitrary packages. So option 2 is not a \`package.json\` edit — it is "teach the engine exports-map resolution", which is a different ticket and a much larger one. This is also precisely why the esbuild bundle exists: \`buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs\` runs with \`bundle: true\`, inlining that subtree into one browser-resolvable file.

**Option 3 (lazy/optional runtime import) — REJECTED, insufficient.** It addresses the runtime consumer and leaves the **build-time** one broken. \`buildScripts/util/templateBuildProcessor.mjs:2\` imports the bundle at *module scope* (its own comment reads \`// parse5 is bundled and available\`), and \`esmodules.mjs\` → \`astTemplateProcessor\` → \`templateBuildProcessor\` means an installed engine dies with \`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND\` before the build starts. Making that lazy too is strictly more change than option 1 for the same outcome, and it would make a build prerequisite conditional.

**Option 1 measurements.** The artifact is **163 KB** (\`dist/parse5.mjs\`, measured — the ~170 KB above was an estimate). \`npm pack --dry-run\` is the authoritative read of what ships, and it confirms the premise from the packing tool rather than from \`.npmignore\`: of **5329** packed files, the only \`parse5\` entry is \`buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs\` (784 bytes — the *producer*, whose inputs a consumer does not have). The bundle itself is absent.

**Why option 1 is the right shape and not merely the smallest:** it is the only option that satisfies the build-time and runtime consumers with one change, because both want the same file at the same path. The objection — a build output in the published tree, interacting with \`#17238\` — is real but narrow: this is one deterministic 163 KB file reproducible from a pinned devDependency, not the generated-history problem \`#17238\` owns.

| release producer | `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs:146` → `buildScripts/build/all.mjs:135` | `npm publish` runs `build-all`, which bundles parse5 before packing | none — unchanged by this ticket, verified by reading both call sites rather than assumed | — | the two call sites |
| `.npmignore` inclusion rule | this ticket | `/dist/*` excludes the tree's contents; `!/dist/parse5.mjs` re-includes exactly one file | a directory-shaped `/dist` rule silently defeats the negation — an ignore rule on a directory is not reversible | inline comment stating that, beside the `/apps/**/*` precedent it copies | reverting to `/dist` reds the guard |
| required-entry guard | this ticket | `REQUIRED_ENTRIES` / `findMissingEntries` in `check-package-contents.mjs` fail the pack when a required artifact is absent | the forbidden-prefix half is unchanged; the two run independently | script JSDoc explaining why presence needs its own gate | four unit arms plus an end-to-end entrypoint mutation |
| CI fidelity | this ticket | the check job bundles parse5 before packing, so the tarball under test is release-shaped | without it the job can only ever test the exclusion half, never presence | workflow step comment | the job red before the step, green after |
| consumer validation | **#17931** | an installed engine builds `dist/esm`, boots, and parses a template through `HtmlTemplateProcessor` | none — it is the only fixture that can observe this | #17931's own ACs | scope-transferred there; not claimed here |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] One of the options above is chosen with its rationale recorded, and the other two are recorded as rejected with why. **Done 2026-08-31 — see Decision above.**
- [x] ~~A consumer-shaped fixture — an engine installed as a package, not this checkout — builds `dist/esm` and the emitted `HtmlTemplateProcessor` import resolves.~~ **Scope-transferred to #17931**, which owns the installed-engine fixture this requires; it could never be satisfied from here.
- [x] ~~`HtmlTemplateProcessor` loads and parses a template in that consumer output.~~ **Scope-transferred to #17931**, same reason — it needs that fixture's output to run in.
- [ ] If option 1 is chosen, a spec asserts the artifact is in the packed set — `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` already owns that surface — so a future `.npmignore` edit cannot silently drop it again.
- [ ] The build-time consumer (`templateBuildProcessor.mjs`) is unaffected either way.

## Out of Scope

- #17942 — the guard corrections and the in-repo copy. This ticket does not change that copy; it decides what a consumer gets.
- #17238 — the pack-size consequence of what ships. Relevant input to option 1, not this ticket's decision.
- #17931 — the boot arm. It would exercise this, but a consumer-install fixture is a different shape from a workspace fixture.

## Avoided Traps

- **Exempting the specifier in the guard.** It is a real broken import in the output tree. Silencing it restores the pre-#17921 state, where the failure simply waited for a runtime.
- **Copying the bundle from `node_modules/neo.mjs/dist/`.** Measured: that directory is not published, so the copy has no source. A fallback that reads a path nothing writes is a silent no-op.
- **Treating this as a `dist/esm` defect.** Webpack builds resolve it today because they bundle from this repository; the gap is what an installed engine carries, so a `dist/esm`-only fix would leave the same hole for any other consumer of `src/`.
